a: Prins, C., Prodhon, C., Wolfler Calvo, R.
t: A memetic algorithm with population management (MA|PM) for the capacitated location-routing problem
v: Evolutionary Computation in Combinatorial Optimization (EvoCOP 2006), LNCS 3906:183–194
n: MA|PM: chromosome = depot-status vector plus customer sequence cut into routes by Split; one-point crossover with repair; offspring are accepted only if their distance to the population exceeds a threshold. Local search LS1 (MOVE, SWAP, OPT, first improvement) or a light LS2 without moves between routes of different depots; a depot can be opened only by the crossover. Sets P, T and B (Barreto); one run per instance. Rounding of distances and code availability not stated; conclusion says the method is not yet definitively tuned.

a: Prins, C., Prodhon, C., Ruiz, A., Soriano, P., Wolfler Calvo, R.
t: Solving the capacitated location-routing problem by a cooperative Lagrangean relaxation-granular tabu search heuristic
n: LRGTS: Lagrangean relaxation for the depot phase, granular tabu search (single-node transfer) for the routing phase, then a first-improvement local search with MOVE, SWAP and OPT (2-opt within a route or between routes). Creators of the P set: states that the P distances are multiplied by 100 and rounded up, and that B and T distances are not rounded.

a: Duhamel, C., Lacomme, P., Prins, C., Prodhon, C.
t: A GRASP×ELS approach for the capacitated location-routing problem
n: GRASP with evolutionary local search; first-improvement MOVE, SWAP and OPT neighbourhoods.

a: Yu, V. F., Lin, S.-W., Lee, W., Ting, C.-J.
t: A simulated annealing heuristic for the capacitated location routing problem
n: Simulated annealing on a giant-tour-like string with depots and dummy zeros. Random moves: insertion, swap and a modified 2-opt (each with probability 1/3), all of which may involve depot nodes; after each temperature step a swap and an insertion local search is applied to the best solution. States that P distances are multiplied by 100 and rounded up, and that B and T distances are not rounded. No code or data availability statement. Future research: other multi-level problems (hub location, multimodal).

a: Escobar, J. W., Linfati, R., Toth, P.
t: A two-phase hybrid heuristic algorithm for the capacitated location-routing problem
n: Granular tabu search in the improvement phase; Shift, Swap and inter-tour exchange moves.

a: Jarboui, B., Derbel, H., Hanafi, S., Mladenović, N.
t: Variable neighborhood search for location routing
n: VNS for a variant of the problem: capacitated depots and one uncapacitated vehicle per depot (vehicle capacity is not considered), so it is not the CLRP. Five neighbourhoods, each intra- and inter-route: insertion, swap, extended Or-opt (segment moved in order), inverse Or-opt (segment moved reversed; 2-opt is a special case) and add/drop depot (close one open depot, open a closed one). Sequential or mixed VND; random or semi-random shaking; time limit n/2 s. Rounding and code not stated. Future work: adapt the method to the CLRP.

a: Derbel, H., Jarboui, B., Chabchoub, H., Hanafi, S., Mladenović, N.
t: A variable neighborhood search for the capacitated location-routing problem
n: VNS with VND for the CLRP (capacitated depots and vehicles). Neighbourhoods: insertion, reassignment of a route to another open or closed depot, swap, insertion of a segment (Or-opt and inverse Or-opt) and exchange of two segments in four orientations; capacity violations are penalised. Tested on Barreto’s set only (costs not rounded); reaches almost all best values of SALRP. Code not stated.

a: Ting, C.-J., Chen, C.-H.
t: A multiple ant colony optimization algorithm for the capacitated location routing problem
n: MACO: nested colonies for location selection, customer assignment and routing. Local search on the best solution of each iteration: 2-opt (two non-consecutive arcs, within a route or between two routes), swap and insertion (same or different route), then insertion and swap between two open depots, best improvement. 94 instances (Perl 9, Barreto 19, Prins 30, Tuzun-Burke 36), 10 runs; mean gap 0.36% on the P set. Rounding and code not stated. Future research: checking depot capacity during assignment, shared control parameters, reliable location routing, other multi-level problems. Read: method, local search, instances and conclusions.

a: Contardo, C., Cordeau, J.-F., Gendron, B.
t: A GRASP + ILP-based metaheuristic for the capacitated location-routing problem
n: GRASP builds a bundle of solutions, an ILP recombines their routes, and a column-generation local improvement follows. The local search cycles through seven procedures in a fixed order: facility open, facility swap, giant-tour split, route swap (first improvement); 2-opt with 2-exchange and 2-opt* (best improvement); 3-opt (first improvement). 89 instances, 10 runs each; improves the best known value on 17. Rounding and code release not stated. Future research: the two-echelon CLRP and the two-echelon CVRP.

a: Löffler, M., Bartolini, E., Schneider, M.
t: A conceptually simple algorithm for the capacitated location-routing problem
n: GRASP with a 13-operator VND (Table 1) and a depot-configuration refinement; operator ablation on the P, B and T sets.

a: He, P., Hao, J.-K., Wu, Q.
t: A hybrid genetic algorithm with multi-population for capacitated location routing
n: HGAMP. Source of many best known values used on this site. Read from the authors’ own manuscript copy (not the published layout; targeted extraction): variable neighbourhood descent with ten granular moves from Duhamel et al. (2010) and Schneider and Löffler (2019) (relocate one or two consecutive customers, swap variants, intra-route 2-opt, two 2-opt* variants); depots change only through crossover, mutation and repair. 281 instances (B 13, P 30, T 36, S 202), 20 runs each. The text does not state the distance rounding. Source code is public (see the repository record). Future research: periodic location routing, two-echelon routing, location-arc routing.

a: He, P., Hao, J.-K., Wu, Q.
t: Code and data repository for “A hybrid genetic algorithm with multi-population for capacitated location routing”
v: INFORMS Journal on Computing (code and data repository)
n: Open code and data of HGAMP: https://github.com/INFORMSJoC/2023.0416. MIT License, copyright 2025 Pengfei He, Jin-Kao Hao and Qinghua Wu (LICENSE file read). The README lists the benchmark instances, the source code, detailed results and the best solutions (certificate file); it does not mention distance rounding. The instance and certificate files themselves were not opened here.

a: Zou, Y., Hao, J.-K., Wu, Q.
t: A reinforcement learning guided hybrid evolutionary algorithm for the latency location routing problem
n: Latency variant (LLRP), not the CLRP. Its VND uses seven neighbourhoods (relocate, swap, 2-opt / 2-opt*, relocate of two consecutive customers, customer-arc swap, arc-arc swap, SWAP*) restricted to the nearest vertices, and compares a random order and a fixed order with a Q-learning order. Instances and best solutions: https://github.com/YujiZou/LLRP (stated in the paper); the code is announced, the data availability statement says on request.
